title: Your Horoscope This Week: August 30 To September 5
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: August 30 To September 5

R29 babes, you made it through the eclipse threshold, and this week is about slowing down enough to understand what just changed. In the days after the Pisces lunar eclipse, emotions may still be settling and certain realizations may need time before they make complete sense. As August ends, Jupiter in Leo forms a supportive fire trine with Saturn in Aries, bringing the planet of luck and expansion into harmony with the planet of discipline and responsibility. This is the universe reminding us that bold dreams and practical effort can exist in the same room, and that the work we’ve been doing is creating real protection around the next chapter. Opportunities may feel more solid, confidence may return, and something that once felt risky could suddenly seem much more possible. Take the win, cosmic beings. You survived the emotional group project, and now the cosmos is handing everyone snacks.

The beginning of September is relatively calm, with no major transits until the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini on September 4th. Last Quarter Moons are checkpoints of release and recalibration, helping us decide what still matters after the Full Moon’s revelations and what can be left behind. A week ago, we were deep in our feelings; now the Gemini Moon offers perspective, peaceful detachment, curiosity, and enough playfulness to remember that one difficult chapter does not have to become our entire personality. Laugh when you can, and let yourself view the eclipse story from a little farther back. What a difference a week can make.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, August ends with the kind of cosmic support that helps you remember what happens when confidence and discipline work together. Jupiter in Leo is energizing your romance, creativity, fame, fate, and inner child realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in your sign, making it easier to turn inspiration into something real. The ideas, risks, relationships, or creative goals that survived eclipse season now have stronger foundations beneath them. Put yourself out there, accept the invitation, share the work, or make the first move. You don’t need to choose between being bold and being responsible this week; the more seriously you take your joy, the more momentum it can create.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini activates your communication and mindset zone, helping you process everything that shifted over the past week. A conversation, thought pattern, or piece of information may look very different now that the emotional intensity of the Pisces eclipse has settled. Let go of the need to explain yourself perfectly, replay every exchange, or turn one uncertain moment into a permanent conclusion. The Gemini Moon brings perspective, so change your mind where needed and choose the words that create movement instead of keeping you stuck in the same mental loop.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, August ends by helping you strengthen your inner foundation before making your next move. Jupiter in Leo is expanding your home, family, roots, and emotional security realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your solitude and closure zone. This can bring progress around a move, family decision, healing process, or the private work you’ve been doing to feel safer within yourself. You may finally understand that creating a better home life also requires releasing old fears, guilt, or habits that keep you emotionally stuck. Clear out a room, set a boundary with family, rest without apologizing for it, or make one concrete decision that gives your future self more peace.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini activates your money and security sector, helping you reassess what’s actually worth your time, energy, and spending after eclipse season. A financial concern may feel less overwhelming once you look at it with fresh eyes, or you may realize that one expense, subscription, or income plan no longer makes sense. Review your budget, follow up on a payment, sell what you no longer use, or brainstorm a more flexible way to earn. The Gemini Moon wants options, so release the belief that there is only one path to stability and let yourself experiment with a smarter one.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, you made it through eclipse season, and August ends by reminding you that your voice can open doors when the right people are listening. Jupiter in Leo is expanding your communication, writing, learning, and media realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your friendship, community, and social network zone. A conversation, introduction, collaboration, or idea shared online could lead somewhere substantial now, especially if you have been consistent about showing up and refining your message. The vibe is less “crying in the notes app” and more “wait, this could actually work.”

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in your sign helps you step back and recognize how much you’ve changed since last week’s Pisces eclipse. You may feel ready to release an identity, expectation, look, habit, or personal storyline that no longer fits, especially if you have been shape-shifting to keep everyone else comfortable. Gemini energy gives you permission to update the narrative without turning it into a full press conference. Keep what still feels true, let the rest expire, and enter the weekend with more curiosity about who you’re becoming than attachment to who you used to be.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, you made it through this month’s eclipses, and August ends with real momentum around money, purpose, and the career structure you’ve been building. Jupiter in Leo is expanding your income and security realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your career and public image zone. This can look like a financial opportunity becoming more stable, a professional decision finally making sense, or greater confidence in what your work is worth. Use this week to take one serious step toward the income level you keep envisioning. The emotional fog’s lifting, and the universe is saying “okay, now let’s make it sustainable.”

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your spirituality, closure, and subconscious realm, giving you space to process everything the Pisces eclipse stirred up. You may notice that one fear, regret, or mental loop has less power over you than it did a week ago. Release the need to find a perfect explanation for every feeling, and give yourself permission to rest, journal, pray, unplug, or sit in silence without turning solitude into isolation. The Gemini Moon helps you loosen your grip on the story and keep only the lesson.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, you made it through eclipse season, and August ends with your confidence returning alongside a much clearer sense of where you’re headed next. Jupiter in your sign is expanding your identity, visibility, and personal goals while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your travel, education, publishing, and expansion realm. A bold idea can start feeling much more realistic now because you’re finally willing to give it structure. The universe is supporting the version of you who dreams big and also reads the fine print, which is growth.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini activates your friendship, community, and social network zone, helping you reassess who belongs in this next chapter. One week after the Pisces eclipse, you may have more perspective on which friendships feel reciprocal, which group dynamics have become distracting, and where you’ve been seeking approval from people who aren’t even paying that much attention. Use this week to clear out the stale group chats, follow up with the collaborators who inspire you, and release the pressure to be everywhere at once. Your next era needs community, Leo, but it does not need an audience of random spectators.

Virgo Sun & Rising:

Virgo, how does it feel to come through the final eclipse of the year during your own birthday season and realize that you’re entering this new chapter with a very different understanding of yourself? Jupiter in Leo is expanding your spirituality, healing, and behind-the-scenes realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your intimacy, transformation, and shared-resources zone. This can help you make sense of the emotional, financial, or relational weight you’ve been carrying and see where greater trust, structure, or support is finally becoming possible. You may feel ready to close out an old fear, become more intentional about what you share with others, or make a private decision that strengthens your sense of inner stability.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini brings a checkpoint to your career, reputation, and long-term goals. One week after the Pisces eclipse may have shifted your perspective on relationships, you could now feel more aware of how much your public life has been shaped by trying to meet everyone else’s expectations. This weekend may leave you wanting to rethink the way you present yourself professionally, refine a goal that has become too rigid, or step away from a role that no longer reflects who you’re becoming. Give yourself room to experiment with a new direction and let clarity build through movement.

Libra Sun & Rising:

Libra, now that you’re on the other side of the Pisces eclipse, you may be realizing just how much your daily life affects the way you show up in relationships, work, and even your own body. Jupiter in Leo’s expanding your friendship, community, and long-term goals realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your partnership zone, creating a rare sense that the right people can actually help you build something lasting. A friendship may become more serious, a collaboration may begin to feel reliable, or a relationship could start aligning more naturally with the future you want. This is a strong moment to notice who follows through, who brings substance to your ideas, and where support is becoming mutual instead of symbolic.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your travel, education, publishing, and expansion zone, helping you step back from the emotional intensity of the past week and look at the bigger picture. You may find yourself reconsidering a trip, course, belief, or long-term plan, especially if it was shaped by pressure rather than curiosity. This weekend is less about locking in one grand answer and more about letting your perspective become flexible again, so give yourself room to explore, ask different questions, and remember that changing your mind can be part of moving forward.

Scorpio Sun & Rising:

Scorpio, now that the Pisces eclipse has stirred your heart, creativity, and inner child, the end of August helps you turn what you felt into something you can actually build. Jupiter in Leo’s expanding your career, visibility, and long-term ambitions while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in the area of wellness and daily responsibility. This can bring a rare sense that your professional growth is no longer competing with the structure your life requires; the two can begin supporting each other. A goal that once felt too large may now seem achievable because you can finally see the practical steps between where you are and where you want to be.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your intimacy, shared-resources, and transformation realm, helping you gain perspective on an emotional or financial entanglement that felt heavier during eclipse week. You may find yourself reconsidering what you owe, what you share, how much access someone has to you, or whether a bond still feels reciprocal beneath the intensity. Gemini energy gives you enough distance to talk through what’s been difficult to name and consider more than one solution, rather than assuming everything must end in a dramatic all-or-nothing decision. Let the weekend show you where a lighter agreement, clearer boundary, or more honest conversation could release pressure without requiring you to shut down.

Sagittarius Sun & Rising:

Sagittarius, the emotional weight of the Pisces eclipse may still be settling, especially around home, family, or your sense of belonging, but the end of August helps you remember that your life is still expanding beyond what feels uncertain right now. Jupiter in Leo is energizing your zone of travel, education, and long-term vision while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your creativity, romance, and inner child realm. This is a beautiful reminder that your biggest dreams can become more real when you give them shape, discipline, and time. You may feel called to recommit to a creative project, take a romantic risk with greater maturity, or finally treat an idea you love like something worth building rather than something you visit only when inspiration strikes.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your partnership zone, helping you look at your closest relationships with more perspective and less emotional fog. One week after the eclipse may have brought up questions about where you feel at home and who helps create that feeling with you, this weekend could lead to an important conversation about expectations, reciprocity, or the future of a bond. You may also notice that you’re ready to release the need for every relationship
to fit one fixed definition. Let curiosity guide the conversation, listen for what’s changed, and allow the connection to evolve without forcing an immediate verdict.

Capricorn Sun & Rising:

Capricorn, the Pisces eclipse may have left you with a lot to think about, but the end of August gives you a much stronger sense of what needs to be handled privately before you can move forward with confidence. Jupiter in Leo is expanding your intimacy, shared-resources, and transformation realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your home, family, and emotional foundation zone. This can help you make meaningful progress around a shared financial plan, a housing decision, a family responsibility, or a deeper conversation about trust and support. You may realize that the stability you want cannot come only from holding everything together by yourself. The more honest you are about the support you need, the easier it becomes to build a life that feels secure on every level.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your work, wellness, and daily routine realm, helping you release some of the pressure that’s accumulated around being productive all the time. You may find yourself wanting to reorganize your schedule, rethink how much you take on in a single day, or create more flexibility around habits that have become too rigid to be useful. This weekend’s a good time to notice where your routine supports your energy and where it simply keeps you busy, because the lighter Gemini influence can help you find a smarter way forward without turning every adjustment into another serious life overhaul.

Aquarius Sun & Rising:

Aquarius, the Pisces eclipse may have brought a financial or self-worth realization that’s still settling, but the end of August reminds you that the right relationships can help you move forward with much more confidence. Jupiter in Leo is expanding your partnership realm while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your communication zone, making this an excellent time for honest conversations that lead somewhere constructive. A romantic partner, collaborator, client, or close friend may help you clarify an idea, strengthen a commitment, or see a possibility you had been too overwhelmed to recognize during eclipse week.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your creativity, romance, fate, and inner child realm, bringing a lighter checkpoint after such an emotionally charged month. You may realize that a crush, creative project, or personal dream has become burdened by too many expectations, and this weekend gives you permission to reconnect with the original spark that made it exciting. Let yourself experiment without needing every idea to become a business plan or every romantic interaction to become a life decision. The more playfully you approach what comes next, the easier it’ll be to recognize which desires still feel alive and which ones you’re ready to release.

Pisces Sun & Rising:

Pisces, last week’s lunar eclipse in your sign may have left you feeling like you shed an entire version of yourself overnight, and the end of August helps you understand what this rebirth is asking you to build next. Jupiter in Leo is expanding your work, wellness, and daily routine zone while forming a supportive trine with Saturn in Aries in your money, security, and self-worth sector. This is the kind of energy that helps you turn a personal realization into a more sustainable life, whether that means creating healthier habits, asking for better pay, restructuring your workload, or becoming more disciplined about where your time and energy go. You may still feel emotionally tender, but this alignment reminds you that small, responsible choices can protect the new version of you that eclipse season just revealed.

Then, on September 4th, the Last Quarter Moon in Gemini moves through your home, family, and roots realm, helping you reassess what you need to feel emotionally safe and supported. You may find yourself wanting to change your space, have a family conversation, release an old childhood narrative, or become more honest about where you no longer feel at home. Gemini energy brings perspective, so you don’t have to make every feeling mean that your whole foundation is falling apart. Let yourself consider new ways of creating belonging, and allow home to become something flexible enough to grow with you.

title: R29 Editors Are Obsessing Over Lululemon Bags—These Are, Hands Down, The Best
text:
R29 Editors Are Obsessing Over Lululemon Bags—These Are, Hands Down, The Best

Lululemon knows a thing or two about creating viral belt bags, chic travel accessories, and conversation-starting tote bags. The R29 reader-favorite brand also knows how to do them especially well, with most bag styles receiving at least 4 out of 5 stars from thousands of devout customers.

And there’s a whole lot of range and variety. From sporty fanny packs and versatile crossbody bags to spacious carryalls and backpacks, Lululemon has all your everyday essentials… and concert outfit and vacation plan needs covered!

Read on to shop bag styles from Lululemon’s bestsellers, as well as in-demand new arrivals with already-stellar reviews.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Lululemon Backpacks

A trusty backpack is essential for any fitness or everyday wardrobe — and Lululemon has a variety of high-quality packs to choose from. “For years, Lululemon’s Everyday Backpack was my go-to travel pack,” R29’s senior writer Karina Hoshikawa says. “The design is sleek and streamlined, but don’t be fooled: The backpack can hold a ton of stuff. I also love that it has plenty of compartments and pockets (but not too many that things inevitably get lost), and has a padded pocket that fits my 15-inch work laptop. It’s also made from a water-repellent, recycled nylon fabric that is surprisingly easy to clean in case of accidental spills. I use it mostly for travel, but I truly could see this working perfectly for everyday use (hence the name), commutes, or school.”

For fans of the beloved Everywhere Belt Bag, don’t sleep on its sibling, the spacious Everywhere Backpack: It’s a classic style, with durable ripstop fabric (not to mention, 100% of the polyester is recycled material). Heading out for a hike or long bike ride? The highly rated All Sport Backpack is ready for any outdoor adventure, with plenty of space for gear and hydration. Or, for something a bit more versatile, the Wunderlust Backpack Mini is a great pick. 

Shop Lululemon Bags

title: I Tried GapStudio’s Fall Denim-Forward Collection—& I Have Thoughts
text:
I Tried GapStudio’s Fall Denim-Forward Collection—& I Have Thoughts

I’m a self-declared Gap girl, so I was super eager to preview GapStudio‘s fall collection, which launches today. The premium clothing line under Gap and Zac Posen’s direction has entered its second fall season with a capsule of elevated denim, matching sets, workwear, and wardrobe essentials. “It’s a natural evolution of the language we’ve been building at GapStudio, but this season, we pushed proportion and construction much further,” Posen tells Refinery29.

The new womenswear and menswear collections unsurprisingly complement each other, both inspired by turn-of-the-century American workwear, according to Posen. “The collection is inherently gender-fluid. I was interested in creating a shared wardrobe where menswear and womenswear inform one another and the pieces can move naturally between the two,” he adds. “Ultimately, it’s about giving people beautifully considered clothes with a strong point of view and the freedom to create their own character through them.”

Ahead, I try the GapStudio womenswear collection and share my honest opinions about the look, feel, and sizing of the limited-edition pieces so you can confidently cart up your favorites (before they sell out) and build trendy fall outfits.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Crop Canvas Jacket, Belted Utility Pants & Poplin Fitted Shirt

Cutting right to the chase, this deep indigo matching set was my absolute favorite and is my top recommendation to cart up. It’s especially great if you’re petite and curvy since GapStudio only offers standard sizing and lengths, and us shorties want to get in on the action!

I was completely shocked when this set felt like it was tailored to my body. “Seaming, volume, and structure are built into the architecture of the garments, so the construction becomes part of their character and the way they sit on the body,” Posen explains. As a curvy gal (currently with a 33-inch waist and 46-inch hips), it can be hard to find pants that fit right in all the right places. But these ones did, with a size 31/12 cinching my waist even before tightening the matching belt. And standing at just 5 feet and 3 inches tall, I surprisingly wasn’t swallowed by the wide-leg pants, especially when paired with a wedge.

The matching jacket similarly fit great in a size large, and I found the cropped proportion to be very flattering both when worn opened or buttoned up. It gives the vibe of an elevated denim jacket, and as a whole outfit, a Canadian tuxedo, sans any denim (but more on that below!).

I also really loved pairing the pants with this button-down top, which was my favorite top of the collection. The fitted torso hugged my waist and felt more feminine than a typical button-down top. Plus, the exaggerated puffed sleeves added more dimension and extra interest to an otherwise (let’s face it, boring) wardrobe staple.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Printed Denim Sweatshirt & Pleated Parachute Pants

It took me quite a few glances when previewing images of this sweatshirt online to realize that it was in fact a sweatshirt and not a denim jacket. Posen notes: “There are playful moments of trompe l’oeil inspired by archival Gap pieces, taking something incredibly familiar and shifting the perception of it through print, fabrication, and construction.” And after a fascination with faux-denim sweatpants in the last few years, I foresee this piece going viral too. The distressed denim wash and nearly-metallic button prints were trippy in all the best ways. The heavy fabric and oversized fit were also super comfortable — I opted for a size large again.

I paired the top with cargo-inspired parachute pants. These were definitely more snug and required some serious maneuvering over my hips because of a slimmer waistband. There are adjustable straps and buckles on both sides that allow you to adjust the waist and customize to your comfort level. But even so, I think sizing up to a 14 would have been better. Overall, I really enjoyed the utilitarian-style buckles, oversized back pockets, and adjustable cinched hems of these pants.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Double-Pocket Denim Jacket & High Rise Pintuck Jeans

Though it was hard for Posen to pick his favorite GapStudio pieces, he shares: “I love the full denim-on-denim look with the Pintuck Flare Jean and Double Pocket Jacket.”

This elevated Canadian tuxedo definitely made a statement, though it did feel too big for me. With a different sizing chart, I opted for the size 33/16R, which did fit my waist and hips (though with some back gaping), but the flared fit was too long for little ol’ me, pooling around my feet, even in heels. But I can see these becoming a tall-girl approved jean! I really appreciated the elevated front and back pintucks and the super-flattering seams above the back pockets for an exaggerated hourglass shape.

The matching jacket was very cool with its oversized balloon sleeves, front patch pockets, and collar. The versatile dual-ended zipper also allows for re-styling the piece in many ways. But I think because of the baggy fit and XL details, I would’ve preferred to size down to a medium. (Hot tip: It’s also great to layer with the sheer mesh denim printed tee.)

DashDividers_1_500x100

Printed Denim Terry Dress

Yet another deceiving look that impressed me! No, this is not a denim dress, but rather a French terry dress with a hyper-realistic denim print. The size large was perfect for me thanks to the super stretchy fabric. This style may just be the fashion It-girl alternative to wearing a sweater dress this fall. It also feels smart enough to wear to the office without anyone blinking an eye.

So, if you’re ready to add to cart and just need some more styling inspo, Posen suggests: “Mix pieces across menswear and womenswear, layer unexpected shapes together, or put something more architectural against something incredibly familiar. There shouldn’t be too many rules. Clothes are a tool for self-invention.”

title: It’s Gonna Be A Victorian Blouse Fall For Me—Here’s Why
text:
It’s Gonna Be A Victorian Blouse Fall For Me—Here’s Why

I’ve always had a penchant for frilly, awe-inducing things. That applies whether it’s a ruffled baby doll dress or a twirl-worthy skirt. But right now, it’s the Victorian-era inspired tops that are taking up space in my shopping cart. Think subtly sheer fabrics and volume-maxxing sleeves.

Of course, dainty, statement blouses have always been a thing, but I think my newfound love for them started when Chemena Kamali made her debut at Chloé. The unapologetically feminine designs were an instant hit, and, like clockwork, are trickling from the runway and into real life.

On the contemporary side of the aisle, Dôen is leading the pack with charming lace-trimmed creations and gauzy cotton designs that are as romantic as they are comfortable. Similarly, Free People has stayed true to its bohemian-inspired roots, working sheer ethereal tops throughout its pre-fall collection, from a lace number worn by Willow Smith in the new campaign to a billowing ruffle top that’s quickly selling out. And, hate it or love it, Zara never misses. This season, I’ve already scored my very own frill topper from the retailer.

One of the main reasons I’m so drawn to the flirty tops right now is because they are the perfect yin to my yang of casually cool bottoms. Whether it’s a pair of loose-fitting barrel leg jeans, comfy drawstring trousers, or baggy Bermuda shorts it balances out those boyishly cool pieces like no other top can do.

During Copenhagen Fashion Week, showgoers showed us how it’s done with a mixture of longline shorts and voluminous jeans. What really took their looks to the next level was the finishing touches. Think cool sunglasses, coin purse necklaces, and classic hats. For shoes, street style stars anchored the trend wearing kitten heels, platforms, and wedges.

If you’re thinking about having a romantically chic fall, a frilly top is all your closet needs. Here, shop our favorite Victorian-inspired, ruffle blouses on the market.

title: Plum Perfumes Are Fall’s More Grown-Up Answer To Fruity Scents
text:
Plum Perfumes Are Fall’s More Grown-Up Answer To Fruity Scents Fruity fragrances often get a reputation for being twee, but we promise this fall’s take on the category will have you thinking otherwise. While popular fruity notes typically skew tropical or berry-forward, there’s a new fruit in town this season: plum.

The succulent stone fruit has the same juicy quality as peach, only with a darker, richer flavor profile that makes it especially well-suited to cooler weather. Depending on how it’s blended, plum can read candied and sweet, tart and juicy, or even slightly smoky and boozy, giving perfumers plenty of ways to interpret the note. It also has a natural depth that makes it feel a little more grown-up than your typical fruit-forward fragrance, especially when paired with contrasting accords like woods, amber, spice, or musk. 

From Ellis Brooklyn’s just-launched Plum Tonic to Valentino’s newest addition to its Donna Born In Roma family, we’re calling it now: Plum scents are about to be everywhere. Whether you like your fragrances juicy and playful or dark and sultry, there’s a plum perfume for you to try this fall.

title: 5 Nike Outfits That Nail The Athlete Off-Duty Trend
text:
5 Nike Outfits That Nail The Athlete Off-Duty Trend

Whether you’re catching an early morning flight, running errands around town, or grabbing an iced matcha post-workout, the athlete off-duty aesthetic continues to dominate casually cool moments. It’s the art of looking effortlessly put-together while leaning heavily into performance-worthy gear typically reserved for competitive jocks. The key to nailing it isn’t just throwing on a pair of sweatpants. It’s about unexpected proportions, a splash of tailoring, and clever styling details that take you from the gym floor to the streets without looking slouchy.

In need of some outfit inspo? Ahead, find five Refinery29-approved ways to nail the athlete off-duty trend, courtesy of Nike.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Bermuda Shorts + Tank Top

Nothing feels cooler right now than a pair of longline shorts. We’ve waxed poetic about Bermuda shorts over and over again. But if you’re looking for a way to sportify the trend, these utilitarian babies are the perfect place to start. The key is to balance the oversized proportions with a fitted top like the one-shoulder design here. Electrifying green hues make the outfit pop even more, especially when you finish off the look with a pair of timeless Air Max sneakers.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Capris + Cardigans

Cropped leggings and capris are making a definitive comeback, but the secret to making them look polished is with a classic cardigan. This ribbed knit design looks undeniably cooler when you leave a few of the bottom buttons undone. Bonus points if you wear yours with statement-making flats similar to the lace-up style shown here.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Cropped Jacket + Midi Skirt

One of the most reliable style tips I’ve ever received is to always buy the matching piece. Even if you’re planning to initially wear an item on its own, having the coordinating set makes getting dressed easier. This fall, try swapping your usual sweatpants for a sweat skirt and a matching jacket. Butter yellow sneakers will give any outfit that fun wow factor we love so much. Finish the outfit with crisp white crew socks and a bright white top for instant street-style polish.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Graphic Tee + Denim Shorts

Oversized long-sleeve graphic tees will immediately give you that borrowed-from-the-boys vibe, especially when draped over a long pair of shorts. Make the 2000s aesthetic really come to life with futuristic metallic sneakers and performance-level shield glasses.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Culottes + Quarter-Zips

For a refined, architectural approach to athleisure, contrast a boxy quarter-zip pullover or windbreaker with dramatic, wide-leg billowing culottes. Neutral monochrome tones keep the voluminous silhouette balanced, while clean, minimal sneakers round out the effortlessly elevated look.
